title: Does a purpose-built nailing gantry beat a stock humanoid at fastening sheathing, and at what house volume does it pay?
summary: Designs the machine the earlier buildbot projects point to: a two-axis bridge with a nailer over a flat panel table. On the 62-nail schedule of a 4x8 sheet from buildbot-fasten, 1 m/s axes, 3 m/s2 and 0.5 s a nail give 61 s a sheet, 6.1× faster than hand nailing at the taskbook's minutes; over the sweep 20 to 115 s. The nail windows need a total tip scatter under 1.24 mm, so finding the studs, not the axes, takes the budget. Nailing is 3.3 crew-hours on the walls and 9.0 with roof cassettes ($125 and $341 a house at a $37.86 loaded hour), so a $100k machine breaks even at about 150 houses a year (walls) or 55 (with roof); over a sweep the median is 326 and 120. The H1 saves money in 0.4% of draws on the same wall hours, the G1 cannot take them, and neither reaches the roof. Machine price, load and scan times, axis performance and operator share are swept, not sourced; no machine is built or quoted and the hand minutes are the taskbook author's estimate.
lede: does a purpose-built nailing gantry beat a stock humanoid at fastening sheathing? A modelled two-axis bridge nails a 62-nail sheet in 61 s (6.1x hand nailing); a $100k machine needs about 150 houses a year to break even on walls (50 with roof cassettes), where the H1 saves money in 0.4% of draws (price and times swept, not sourced).
